This history records maintenance changes to this fork by date. Official Rhino release history remains in the upstream release notes and is not presented as new releases of this fork.

[Read the original official Rhino README](https://github.com/mozilla/rhino/blob/d878324a6f515c09d8ca49005fdd22b944b4df89/README.md). This entry is pinned to commit `d878324a6f515c09d8ca49005fdd22b944b4df89`, preserving the upstream language and the context of relative links. The original document is retained without translation; this page and its other language versions describe this fork.

# 2026-11-03

###### 2026/11/03

* `Fix` Promises work with several threads: a reaction added while another thread settles a `NativePromise` is no longer lost, and an embedder can override `Context.forwardTask` to settle on a thread with an event loop and to resume `await` on the thread of its async function

# 2026-11-02

###### 2026/11/02

* `Feature` `async` / `await`: async functions, methods and arrow functions return a native `Promise`, and the code after `await` continues in a microtask; both interpreted and compiled modes
* `Feature` `for await` and async generators (`async function*`), `Symbol.asyncIterator`, `yield*` delegating to async and sync iterators, and async methods in classes and object literals
* `Improvement` Embedding: `AsyncTracker` reports the number of suspended async functions and the first suspension point, and `UnhandledRejectionTracker` is now per `Context`, so script threads no longer see each other's rejections
* `Fix` Nested `try` in generators in compiled mode: the outer `catch` missed the exception when the inner block rethrew it or had a `yield` in its `finally`
* `Fix` A strict function body resumed in a generator took the strictness of its caller; it now always runs with its own
* `Fix` `Promise.all` / `Promise.race` / `Promise.any` read `resolve` before the iterator and reject when that throws; a throwing `then` getter now rejects instead of propagating
* `Fix` `new Function` builds its source as the specification says: a parameter ending in a `//` comment no longer fails and generators read `function*`; `Function.prototype.toString` works on a callable `Proxy`
* `Fix` Optional chains short-circuit as a whole: `a?.b.c` is `undefined` when `a` is `null` or `undefined`, and later indexes and arguments are not evaluated. Only `?.` tests its value, so `a?.b.c` throws a TypeError when `a.b` is `undefined`, and `a?.b()` throws one when the method is missing. `eval?.()` is an indirect call, `delete a?.b.c` is `true` when it short-circuits, and a tagged template on a chain or `new a?.b()` is a syntax error
* `Fix` `async` function and generator declarations inside a block are block-scoped: they are not visible outside the block and no longer overwrite an outer variable of the same name; plain functions behave as before
* `Fix` In compiled mode, a `yield` or `await` nested in another one runs where it is written in generators and `async` functions: `yield [g(1), yield 'x']` calls `g(1)` first, and `await (u ? await g() : 2)` no longer calls `g()` when `u` is false. `[a, b] = [1, yield 2]` no longer fails with `$0` is not defined
* `Fix` Function declarations in the `case` clauses of a `switch` are initialized on entering the `switch`, so a function declared in a `case` that does not run can be called; in sloppy mode an outer variable of the same name is assigned only when the declaration is reached
* `Fix` In debug mode, scripts with `for-of`, destructuring, `class ... extends` or `for await` no longer fail to compile because their line numbers could not be read
* `Fix` Function declarations in a block work like those of a `switch`: they are initialized on entering the block, and in sloppy mode an outer variable of the same name is assigned only when the declaration is reached, and not at all when a destructuring `catch` parameter binds that name. Labelled function declarations (`l: function f() {}`) are initialized early too

# 2026-10-31

###### 2026/10/31

* `Feature` `class` syntax: class declarations and expressions, `extends` / `super`, instance and static fields, static blocks and private names (`#x`), with `toString` giving the source of the class; both interpreted and compiled modes, `async` methods are left for a later version
* `Feature` Built-in constructors can be extended with `class`: `Error`, `Array`, `Map`, `Set`, `Date`, `RegExp`, the TypedArrays and others create instances from `new.target`, and built-in methods return instances of the subclass
* `Feature` `class` can extend Java classes and interfaces (this fork only): `class X extends java.lang.Thread`, or `class X extends JavaAdapter(Base, I1, I2)` for several interfaces; an instance wraps the Java object, its prototype is `X.prototype`, and it has the members the `WrapFactory` of the host adds to that object
* `Feature` Spread arguments in calls and `new`: `f(...args)`, `o.m(...args)`, `super.m(...args)`, `new F(...args)` (compiling them failed with an internal error before, so the whole script could not run)
* `Fix` Logical assignment `&&=` / `||=` / `??=` not short-circuiting (it always wrote back, calling setters and failing on read-only properties)
* `Fix` Array destructuring, array spread and `for...of` departing from the iteration protocol: destructuring variables did not use iterators (a `Set` or a generator gave undefined), spread did not look up the prototype chain for holes, and iterators were not closed, or closed needlessly, on exit; destructuring a non-iterable array-like object is now a TypeError
* `Fix` `Proxy` and `Reflect` departing from the ES2024 internal methods: forwarding and invariant checks of the traps, a Proxy on the prototype chain, array index keys of `Reflect`, and `__proto__` going through the traps of a Proxy
* `Fix` The `with` statement ignoring `Symbol.unscopables` and resolving a binding more than once, and strict mode code not getting a ReferenceError when assigning to a global binding that was deleted
* `Fix` TypedArray reads and writes, `in`, `delete`, `Object.defineProperty` and key order departing from the specification for canonical numeric string keys (including `NaN` and `-0`)
* `Fix` The set methods of `Set` (`union` and others) departing from the specification in how they read a set-like argument, and `Object.fromEntries` not looking up the prototype chain of an entry
* `Fix` Destructuring defaults having no effect when the target already had a value, and wrong results when converting to a primitive an object whose `valueOf` / `toString` returns null
* `Fix` An unparenthesized `yield` in a generator failing to parse in comma expressions, conditional branches, object spread and computed property names
* `Fix` In compiled mode, `super` reading undefined in an object literal with an inline `__proto__`, and calling a numeric variable throwing VerifyError instead of TypeError
* `Improvement` `BigInt.asIntN` / `BigInt.asUintN`, `setBigInt64` / `setBigUint64` of DataView and BigInt TypedArrays throw TypeError for a Number as the specification says (they converted it before); write `BigInt(x)`
* `Improvement` In strict mode, `class` bodies included, an assignment throws TypeError when the `set` trap of a `Proxy` returns false, and so does writing to an accessor with `set: undefined`
* `Improvement` Array spread `[...a]` and spread arguments take a fast path for dense plain arrays, copying directly when the iterators have not been changed

# 2026-10-24

###### 2026/10/24

* `Feature` `Uint8Array` Base64 and hexadecimal conversion: static methods `fromBase64` / `fromHex` and instance methods `toBase64` / `toHex` / `setFromBase64` / `setFromHex`
* `Fix` A `const` inside a loop body of a function not being rebound on each iteration (the `const` kept the first iteration's value, and `for (const x of a)` gave undefined on every iteration; both interpreted and compiled modes were affected)
* `Fix` The discriminant expression of a `switch` statement seeing `let` / `const` declarations of the same name inside the case block
* `Improvement` Assigning to a `const` under the ES6 language version now throws TypeError in non-strict mode too (previously ignored silently), as the ECMAScript specification requires; language versions 180 and below keep the old behavior
* `Dependency` Sync upstream mozilla/rhino to commit `34abaca89` (2026/10/23)

# 2026-10-20

###### 2026/10/20

* `Fix` `Object.defineProperty` wrongly throwing TypeError for an enumerable property whose configurable is false when the descriptor omits `enumerable` (such as `{ value: 5 }`)

# 2026-10-15

###### 2026/10/15

* `Fix` Argument placeholders and brace escaping in error messages, preventing localized diagnostics from losing context or throwing MessageFormat exceptions
* `Fix` Regular expressions with Unicode property escapes (such as `\p{L}`) throwing UnsupportedOperationException on Android 7.x
* `Improvement` Complete 9 non-English translations for 28 engine error messages covering ArrayBuffer, DataView, TypedArray, regular expressions, destructuring and related features

# 2026-10-13

###### 2026/10/13

* `Feature` Dedicated fork introduction and maintenance history in 10 languages, each retaining an entry to the original official Rhino documentation
* `Improvement` README/CHANGELOG now support offline generation from JSON and templates, with read-only checks and CI validation of documentation consistency
